column4: CDC National Diabetes Statistics Report, data year 2023: 28.8mm adults 18+ with diagnosed diabetes less 1.8mm adults with diagnosed type 1 = 27.0mm. Cross-checks against CDC's own statement that type 2 is 90-95% of diagnosed adult cases, which gives 25.9mm to 27.4mm. Incidence is CDC's 1.5mm adults newly diagnosed in 2023 at the midpoint of that 90-95% share, so it is derived rather than stated
column5: Diagnosed, adults. A further 11.0mm adults have undiagnosed diabetes and are not prescribable, so they are upside on diagnosis rather than pool. 41% of adults with type 2 also have chronic kidney disease, about 11.1mm, which sizes a diabetic kidney label

column4: American Heart Association 2025 statistics update. The 6.7mm figure widely quoted from CDC rests on self-reported heart failure in NHANES 2017 to 2020 and its page predates this. No federal agency publishes a national heart failure incidence count, so incidence is left blank rather than carrying a trade-body figure with no traceable study behind it
column5: Self-reported diagnosed, adults 20+. A growing pool, projected to 8.7mm by 2030 and 11.4mm by 2050, so do not hold it flat across a long forecast. Eligibility is set by ejection fraction, roughly half reduced and half preserved, then by NYHA class

column4: Le MH et al., JAMA Network Open, 16 January 2025, open access, doi 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2024.54707: 33.7% of US adults, 86.3mm, in 2020. A microsimulation calibrated on NHANES 2001-2018, corroborated within 1% by a direct NHANES 2021-2023 elastography measurement of 85.8mm. NHANES is cross-sectional so no incidence exists
column5: Total, not diagnosed, and awareness is very low. DO NOT model an asset off this pool. The label pool is steatohepatitis with moderate to advanced fibrosis: 6.7mm in 2020 rising to 11.7mm by 2050, which is 7.8% of the total. Fibrosis split F0 48.4%, F1 29.1%, F2 14.5%, F3 5.7%, F4 2.2%

column4: CDC Chronic Kidney Disease Surveillance System: about 37mm US adults, roughly 1 in 7. NHANES-measured rather than self-reported
column5: Measured, adults, all stages. Most are stage 3 or earlier and undiagnosed: CDC puts awareness at about 1 in 10 of those affected. A drug label will sit on a stage and an albuminuria band, so eligible_pct carries most of the funnel here

column4: NCHS Health E-Stat 111, NHANES August 2021 to August 2023: the BMI 25 to 29.9 band is 86,594,086 US adults. Deliberately NOT carried as a pool. No drug is labelled for the 25 to 29.9 band alone; the incretin labels are BMI 30 and above, or 27 and above with a weight-related comorbidity, which is the obesity pool this book already prices at 107,592,242
column5: An asset tagged Overweight is an obesity drug and should take the obesity pool. The indication_groups table already pools the two for competition; this row exists to stop the BMI 25 to 29.9 count being read as an addressable population

column4: SEER, Cancer Stat Facts: Lung and Bronchus Cancer. Prevalence is the US count living with the disease; incidence is estimated new cases for the year
column5: All lung cancer, so it is broader than the non-small-cell pool the book already prices separately. An asset tagged this indication rather than the specific histology should be checked before it takes the whole pool

column4: SEER, Cancer Stat Facts: Bladder Cancer. Prevalence is the US count living with the disease; incidence is estimated new cases for the year
column5: Includes non-muscle-invasive disease, which is most of the prevalence and a different treatment setting from muscle-invasive or metastatic. Eligibility is set by stage and by BCG response

column4: SEER, summed across oesophagus, stomach, colorectum, pancreas and anus. The MeSH scope for this term begins at the mouth, and adding oral cavity and pharynx gives 2,328,060 prevalent and 299,090 new cases, which is the wider reading
column5: A container term rather than a disease. Any asset tagged only this should be re-tagged to the site it actually treats before the pool is used

column4: SEER does not publish a prevalence count for fallopian tube cancer separately: it is reported within the ovary, fallopian tube and peritoneum group. New cases of fallopian tube origin are roughly 2,000 to 3,900 a year
column5: Use the combined ovary, fallopian tube and peritoneum pool, about 21,000 new cases a year, for an asset tagged this indication, since that is how the trials enrol and how SEER counts

column4: CDC national lupus registries programme, the five state registries, age-standardised to the US population
column5: Diagnosed. Roughly 90% female. Severity and organ involvement set eligibility, and the renal subset is carried separately below

column4: Derived from the CDC lupus registry prevalence and the registries' own proportion developing nephritis, which is about 35% of systemic lupus patients
column5: Derived rather than stated, so treat it as the weaker of the two lupus rows. Biopsy class drives eligibility

column4: Hunter TM et al., Rheumatology International 2017, PMID 28455559: age-adjusted US prevalence of 0.53% to 0.55% in 2014, applied to the adult population, giving 1,429,747 to 1,483,699. The midpoint is carried. No national incidence count is published
column5: Diagnosed, adults. Eligibility is set by line of therapy: inadequate response to methotrexate, then to a biologic, is where most labels sit

column4: CDC and the Osteoarthritis Action Alliance: about 14mm US adults with symptomatic knee osteoarthritis. No national incidence count is published
column5: Symptomatic, which is the right basis for a treated pool. Kellgren-Lawrence grade and prior treatment failure set eligibility

column4: CDC Community Counts and the Hemophilia Treatment Center Network surveillance. Incidence is births with the disorder a year
column5: Nearly all male. Severity matters enormously for treatment: severe disease, factor VIII below 1%, is about 43% to 60% of the pool depending on the series, and is where prophylaxis products sell

column4: CDC Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System: about 14.2mm US adults with diagnosed COPD. No national incidence count is published
column5: Self-reported diagnosed. The true pool is larger, since COPD is substantially underdiagnosed. Exacerbation history and eosinophil count set eligibility for the newer biologics

column4: Alzheimer's Association 2025 Facts and Figures: 7.4mm Americans aged 65 and over living with Alzheimer's dementia, and about 910,000 new cases a year
column5: Aged 65 and over, clinical dementia. Early and mild disease is where the amyloid-directed labels sit, and amyloid confirmation is a further gate, so eligible_pct is small relative to the pool

column4: National Institute of Mental Health, from the National Survey on Drug Use and Health: 8.3% of US adults had a major depressive episode in the past year
column5: Past-year episode, adults, self-reported through a structured instrument. Treatment-resistant disease, roughly a third of treated patients, is where most new mechanisms are labelled

column4: Wallin MT et al., Neurology 2019, the National MS Prevalence Workgroup: 913,925 US adults, the first national estimate since the 1970s. No national incidence count is published
column5: Adults. Relapsing and progressive forms are counted together here; the progressive subset is carried in the note of its own row rather than as a pool

column4: Parkinson's Foundation Prevalence Project and Willis AW et al. 2022: about 1.1mm Americans, with roughly 90,000 diagnosed a year
column5: Diagnosed. Motor stage and levodopa response set eligibility for add-on therapies

column4: National Institute of Mental Health, from the National Comorbidity Survey Replication. NIMH's widely quoted 2.8% past-year figure is the bipolar SPECTRUM; bipolar I and II, which is what a drug is labelled for, is about 1.4% of adults
column5: Past-year, adults. The spectrum figure would double this pool and should not be used for a labelled indication

column4: National Institute of Mental Health: US prevalence of schizophrenia and related psychotic disorders is estimated between 0.25% and 0.64% across household surveys, clinical interviews and medical records. The midpoint applied to the adult population. No agency publishes a count
column5: A wide range, and the midpoint is carried rather than a stated count, so this is the softest row in the file. The low end gives 674,409 and the high end 1,726,486

column4: Johnson NE et al., the National Myotonic Dystrophy Registry and claims-based studies: about 31,683 with clinically apparent type 1 disease. No national incidence count is published
column5: Clinically apparent type 1. The genetic carrier ceiling is far higher, about 162,690, but most carriers never come to clinical attention and are not a treatable pool

column4: SEER Cancer Stat Facts, myeloma: 36,000 estimated new US cases in 2026. Prevalence equals incidence here by this book's oncology convention: a line of therapy treats the year's diagnoses rather than an accumulating pool, so a patient not started this year has started something else and left the line

Line of therapy sets eligibility: newly diagnosed transplant-eligible, transplant-ineligible and relapsed or refractory are different pools
